extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (persons doing subject-matter-eligibility examination)
extracted.subtask_description: A reference chart for examiners summarizing court decisions relevant to patent subject-matter eligibility; includes citations, patent/app numbers, subject matter summaries, eligibility outcomes, classifications, and cross-references to the 2014 IEG and eligibility examples. Intended to help identify applications that may require detailed eligibility analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case citation and parallel U.S.P.Q. reporter citation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each case (arranged by court and in reverse chronological order), provide a legal citation and, if available, a parallel citation to the U.S.P.Q reporter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the first listed field for each case and is used to identify the decision precisely for further lookup and reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent or application number(s) at issue
rubrics_metrics.description: For each case, list the U.S. patent number(s) or application number(s) that were at issue in the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes all patent numbers or application numbers relevant to the decision so examiners can map a pending file to the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter of the patent/application
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a short description of the title or general subject matter of the patent/application (e.g., methods, systems, products, computer-readable media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to help examiners determine whether a pending application has similar subject matter that might warrant closer eligibility review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility outcome (eligible or ineligible) and scope of finding
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the claims were eligible or ineligible; note that a finding applies to all claims in the patent/application unless otherwise noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the decision distinguishes particular claims (e.g., 'claims 1 & 7-8' or 'claims 2 & 7 eligible'), annotate those specifics. This field signals whether, and to what extent, the decision found claims patent-eligible or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPC and CPC classification
rubrics_metrics.description: List the U.S. Patent Classification (USPC) and Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) codes associated with the patent/application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification information helps examiners identify similar-classified pending applications but, per guidance, similar classification alone does not determine eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference to 2014 IEG / eligibility examples (indexing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A notation of where the case is discussed (if applicable) in the 2014 Interim Eligibility Guidance (IEG) and/or the eligibility examples; an index to the eligibility examples is provided in Appendix 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to point examiners to explanatory sections and worked examples in the 2014 IEG for further analysis and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory that courts did not necessarily use the Alice framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The courts’ analyses in these decisions do not necessarily employ the Alice Corp.-Mayo eligibility framework, which is explained in the Alice Corp.-Mayo (2014 IEG), because most of the cases were decided prior to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should not assume the decision’s reasoning aligns step-for-step with the Alice/Mayo two-part test; adapt the court reasoning into the current eligibility framework when performing analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-specific nature of decisions / limited precedential transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to remember that each case turns on its own facts. Therefore, the mere fact that a pending application may be similarly classified to a patent or an application in this chart, or have similar subject matter, does not necessarily indicate an eligibility issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of similarity is a trigger for further analysis, not a conclusive determination. Examiners should perform a detailed eligibility analysis rather than relying solely on chart similarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial-exception identification triggers further analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of a judicial exception in a claim merely indicates further analysis for eligibility should be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim appears to involve a judicial exception (e.g., abstract idea, law of nature, natural phenomenon), examiners must proceed with the full eligibility analysis rather than stopping at identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chart inclusion criteria and update policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The chart will continue to be updated with Federal Circuit precedential decisions, non-precedential decisions with written opinions and non-precedential decisions originating from the Patent Trial and Appeal Board. Subject matter eligibility affirmances under Fed. Cir. R. 36 will no longer be added to the chart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should treat included decisions as those the chart maintainers consider useful; Fed. Cir. R.36 affirmances are excluded because they 'provide little benefit to examiners.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasive weight of non-precedential written opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: While non-precedential decisions are not binding precedent on the USPTO, the written opinions provide guidance and persuasive reasoning as outlined in Fed. Cir. R. 32.1(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may rely on and cite persuasive reasoning from non-precedential written opinions when conducting exam analyses, but must account for their non-binding status.
